limits: The fixture runtime is synthetic: a C executable named gnome-shell maps four synthetic one-page files at ROOT/lib/libmutter-*.so.0. It does not load or execute Mutter, so native runtime validation, schema/manifest checks, loader resolution, ABI compatibility and compositor capture behaviour are NOT tested. A guard mapping check therefore sees correct synthetic paths and inodes only; it does not establish that a real published runtime is natively valid.
The --runtime argument only supplies the production startup_guard.py module; guard actions run against the private 0700 fixture runtime root under /run/user/UID created by this harness.
No compositor is started, no app is activated, and no GNOME unit, user profile, live desktop bus or session configuration is inspected or changed.

The arm/consume/ready/finish/disarm/status guard actions are exercised against real /proc and real systemd ExecStartPost/ExecStopPost; double-consume concurrency is covered by tests/test_mutter_guard.py instead. Timeout, OOM-kill, missing-finish and power-loss cases are not simulated; the restart cases cover the stale blocked record path, and no case re-arms before restarting.
Service Result/ExecMainCode/ExecMainStatus values are captured from systemd's SERVICE_RESULT/EXIT_CODE/EXIT_STATUS ExecStopPost environment, not inferred.
Linux-only: the harness cannot execute on macOS; only syntax compilation is possible there.
